current_text: Monet painted Rouen Cathedral over thirty times in 1892-93 from rented rooms across the street; he showed twenty at Durand-Ruel in 1895 and sold eight.
new_text: Monet painted Rouen Cathedral's west facade in 1892-93 from rooms facing it, 28 or over thirty times (sources differ); he showed twenty at Durand-Ruel in 1895, priced at 15,000 francs, and some sold.
source_note: Getty: 28 facades, twenty shown 1895; eight-sold unconfirmed

current_text: In 1863 Napoleon III decreed the Salon des Refusés at the Palais de l'Industrie after the jury refused about 2,217 of over 5,000 paintings; more than a thousand people a day came.
new_text: In 1863 Napoleon III ordered the Salon des Refusés at the Palais de l'Industrie after the jury rejected more than half of some 5,000 works submitted; up to 4,000 people came on free Sundays.
source_note: EBSCO: over half of 5,000 rejected; 2,217 was accepted

current_text: In 1779 James Christie valued Robert Walpole's Houghton pictures; the planned sale was cancelled when Catherine the Great bought all 204 works en bloc for £40,555 and sent a ship to fetch them.
new_text: In 1779 Catherine the Great bought Robert Walpole's Houghton pictures en bloc, cancelling a planned sale; James Christie had valued them at £40,000, she paid £40,555 for just over 200 works and sent a ship.

current_text: Renoir's smaller version of Bal du moulin de la Galette (1876) sold at Sotheby's New York on 17 May 1990 for $78.1 million to Ryoei Saito; the large one, Caillebotte's, is in the Orsay.
new_text: Renoir's smaller version of Bal du moulin de la Galette (1876) sold at Sotheby's New York on 17 May 1990 for $78.1 million to Ryoei Saito; the large one, Caillebotte's, is in the Orsay.
source_note: HENI: larger Caillebotte version in Orsay; Guinness confirms $78.1m sale

current_text: Degas's Dans un cafe (1875-76) posed actress Ellen Andree and engraver Marcellin Desboutin at the Nouvelle-Athenes; renamed L'Absinthe in London in 1893, it caused uproar.
new_text: Degas's Dans un cafe (1875-76) posed actress Ellen Andree and artist Marcellin Desboutin at the Nouvelle-Athenes; shown in London in 1893 as L'Absinthe, it caused renewed uproar.
source_note: Apollo + Orsay loan record: Grafton Galleries 1893, renewed furore

current_text: The Cradle (1872) shows Morisot's sister Edma watching her baby Blanche; it failed to sell at the 1874 exhibition, stayed in the family, and entered the Louvre in 1930.
new_text: The Cradle (1872) shows Morisot's sister Edma watching her baby Blanche; it failed to sell at the 1874 exhibition, stayed in the family, and entered the Louvre in 1930.
source_note: Google Arts: unsold at 1874 show, family-held, Louvre 1930

current_text: The Floor Scrapers (1875), set in Caillebotte's flat at 77 rue de Miromesnil, was rejected by the 1875 Salon as vulgar, then shown at the 1876 Impressionist exhibition.
new_text: The Floor Scrapers (1875), probably set in Caillebotte's own studio at 77 rue de Miromesnil, was rejected by the 1875 Salon as vulgar, then shown at the 1876 Impressionist exhibition.
source_note: EGO: probably his studio at 77 rue de Miromesnil

current_text: Bazille was killed on 28 November 1870 at Beaune-la-Rolande, hit twice while leading a failed assault after his officer fell; he was 28, days short of his 29th birthday.
new_text: Bazille was killed on 28 November 1870 at Beaune-la-Rolande, shot twice while leading an assault after his commanding officer was wounded; he was 28, days short of his 29th birthday.
source_note: Art Story: officer injured, led assault, shot twice; 'failed' unconfirmed

current_text: Manet showed Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe at the 1863 Salon des Refusés as 'Le Bain'; its poses come from Raimondi's engraving after Raphael's Judgment of Paris, Victorine Meurent the nude.
new_text: Manet showed Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe at the 1863 Salon des Refusés as 'Le Bain'; its poses come from Raimondi's engraving after Raphael's Judgment of Paris, Victorine Meurent the nude.
source_note: Finestre sull'Arte: Le Bain, Raimondi after Raphael, Victorine Meurent

current_text: Seurat built on Chevreul's 1839 law of simultaneous contrast, found at the Gobelins dye works, and on Ogden Rood's Modern Chromatics, translated into French in 1881.
new_text: Seurat built on Chevreul's 1839 law of simultaneous contrast, found at the Gobelins dye works, and on Ogden Rood's Modern Chromatics, translated into French in 1881.
source_note: Linda Hall Library: Rood translated into French in 1881

current_text: Van Gogh reached Paris in March 1886, shared Theo's flat in rue Laval, moved to 54 rue Lepic in June, met Lautrec, Bernard and Anquetin at Cormon's; he met Gauguin only in November 1887.
new_text: Van Gogh reached Paris in late February 1886, shared Theo's flat in rue Laval, moved to 54 rue Lepic in June, met Lautrec, Bernard and Anquetin at Cormon's; he met Gauguin only in November 1887.
source_note: Van Gogh Museum: arrived late February; Gauguin met November 1887

current_text: The first Impressionist show ran 15 April-15 May 1874 at Nadar's studio, 35 boulevard des Capucines: 30 artists, 165 works, 1 franc entry, about 3,500 visitors.
new_text: The first Impressionist show opened 15 April 1874 for a month at Nadar's old studio, 35 boulevard des Capucines: 30 artists, 165 catalogued works (sources say up to about 200 shown), 1 franc entry, 3,500-4,000 visitors.
